name: UMOD-related autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease
aliases: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to UMOD mutation

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant family history of chronic kidney disease
Identification of pathogenic UMOD gene mutation by genetic testing
Progressive chronic kidney disease with bland urinary sediment and absence of significant proteinuria
History of hyperuricemia and/or early-onset gout
Renal biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy and absence of immune complex deposition

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history, clinical features of tubulointerstitial kidney disease, and confirmation of pathogenic UMOD mutation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; renal biopsy is supportive but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive chronic kidney disease with bland urinary sediment
searchTerms: chronic kidney failure without urine abnormalities
gradual kidney damage with normal urine tests

pathognomonic.notes: Often precedes decline in kidney function

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern of kidney disease

common.symptomName: Polyuria and polydipsia due to impaired urinary concentrating ability
searchTerms: inability to concentrate urine causing polyuria and polydipsia

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

occasional.symptomName: Mild anemia secondary to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: mild low red blood cell count
hard to control high blood pressure
high blood pressure needing many meds

rare.symptomName: Electrolyte disturbances such as metabolic acidosis

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
Hyperuricemia with elevated serum uric acid levels
Bland urinary sediment with minimal proteinuria
imaging: Renal ultrasound may show normal or small kidneys with occasional cysts
other: Renal biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy without immune complex deposition

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in MUC1 gene instead of UMOD
Similar clinical presentation but genetic testing differentiates
Presence of multiple bilateral renal cysts
Mutations in PKD1 or PKD2 genes
More prominent cystic changes on imaging

redFlags: Rapid progression to end-stage renal disease before age 50
Family history of early-onset gout with kidney disease
Unexplained hyperuricemia in young adults with kidney impairment
references: Dahan K et al. UMOD mutations and autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: a review. Kidney Int. 2014;85(4):497-503.
Bleyer AJ et al. Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: diagnosis, classification, and management. Kidney Int. 2017;91(4):1003-1011.
